claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for launch on the present record, relying on aggregate readiness pass and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, with disclosure and monitoring used to justify that certification despite a known loan-modification weakness and an incomplete draft mitigation runbook.
decision_criteria: If the action being audited is clean certification without caveats, the present summary fails the stated policy standard.
If the action is certification only with explicit disclosure plus an already approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence showed the remaining weakness is not material under policy, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence showed the runbook fields are finalized and approved, the verdict could improve.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying release-policy artifact showing how material weakness is defined and how disclosure interacts with certification.
Provide the actual mitigation or risk-acceptance approval, if one exists, including owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Provide the underlying evaluation results for the loan-modification hardship-document checklisting slice, including target, observed score, and launch materiality assessment.
Provide the actual model-card disclosure text proposed for the named launch use case.
Provide the finalized monitoring runbook or dashboard artifact with accountable owner, alert threshold, review cadence/date, and rollback trigger.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself says a current weakness remains in loan-modification hardship-document checklisting.
The policy text says certification without material caveats requires either no material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The actor summary says the runbook is still draft and lacks at least owner and threshold, and also notes review date and rollback criterion still need completion.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk monitoring does not by itself satisfy the enterprise policy predicate for no-caveat certification.
Because evidence access is limited to the actor summary, materiality of the remaining weakness and existence of any approved risk acceptance cannot be independently confirmed.
unsupported_claims: Any clean no-caveat certification is unsupported on the described record.
Any implication that draft monitoring alone removes the current disclosure requirement is unsupported under the quoted policy.
Any implication that public governance guidance substitutes for the policy-required approved mitigation details is unsupported.
